transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Yeah, um… I guess the main thing is I’m just tired all the time. Like, worn out almost every day. I’ll get a full night’s sleep, or at least what should be enough, and when I get up for my cashier shift it’s like my body’s heavy and my head is still dragging.

It’s weird because I used to just need coffee and I’d be okay—there’s this gas station near work that has terrible coffee but I still get it sometimes—but lately even that doesn’t really get me going. So… yeah, that’s why I came in. I’m just feeling run down a lot.
Has this feeling of being run down or tired been present most of the day, nearly every day, for the past couple of weeks?

Yeah, pretty much. I mean, I don’t want to say every single minute, but most days it’s there—like this worn-out feeling almost every day. Even if I sleep a full night, I’ll get up for my cashier shift and my body feels heavy and my head’s still kind of dragging. 

It’s annoying because I keep thinking, “Okay, maybe tomorrow I’ll wake up normal,” and then I’m standing there scanning people’s groceries or whatever and I’m already tired before the day really starts.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

Um… I don’t know. I haven’t really thought about it that way. I mean, I still do stuff when I can, but lately it’s more like I get sidetracked or I’m just thinking about getting through the day.

Like, I used to watch movies after work sometimes, but then I end up scrolling on my phone and next thing I know it’s late, and there’s this one show my coworker keeps telling me to watch—he’s really into those crime shows—but I haven’t gotten around to it. So… I’m not sure if I’d say I’ve lost interest exactly. I guess I haven’t noticed a big change like that.
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or like you’re not good enough lately?

I don’t know… not really in a big way, I guess. Like, I’ll mess something up at work sometimes and feel dumb about it for a while, but I think everyone does that.

Actually, yesterday this guy came through my line with like twelve cans of cat food and I rang one of them twice, and then I was thinking about it way longer than I probably needed to. But I wouldn’t say I’m walking around feeling guilty or like I’m a terrible person or anything. I haven’t really noticed that being a main thing.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past couple of weeks?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed, exactly. Like, I have bad moods, sure, and some days feel kind of blah, but I don’t know if it’s most of the day or nearly every day.

Sometimes I’ll be at work and someone asks how my day’s going and I just say “fine” because it’s easier, and then I start thinking about how weird small talk is, especially when people ask that while I’m bagging their onions or whatever. But… yeah, I don’t think I’ve noticed feeling down all day like that. More just off sometimes, I guess.
Have you noticed yourself moving or thinking more slowly than usual, or feeling like you’re not worth much lately?

Uh… moving slower? I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes I’m slow getting started in the morning, but I’ve always kind of been like that, especially if I’m trying to find clean socks or I realize I forgot to put the trash out.

Thinking slower… I don’t know. At work I still do the register okay. I might overthink stuff, but that’s not really the same, I guess. And feeling like I’m not worth much… no, I wouldn’t really say that. I get annoyed with myself sometimes, but not like that.
Have you noticed that you wake up earlier than usual and can't get back to sleep, or that your sleep doesn't feel restful even if you sleep long enough?

Yeah… I mean, not always waking up super early, exactly. It’s more like I get into bed tired, and then my brain just starts doing that thing where it’s like, okay, bills, and did I check my schedule, and is everybody at home alright, stuff like that.

And then I’ll look at the clock and it’s later than I thought, which is annoying because I was tired. Like last night I was thinking about whether I paid the electric thing or if that’s next week, and then somehow I was also remembering this customer who wanted to argue about coupons, which doesn’t even matter. But yeah, even when I do sleep enough hours, I wake up feeling like I didn’t really settle down. Like I was asleep, but not really rested.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to think clearly, concentrate, or make decisions lately?

Yeah, a little. Like at the register, I can be looking right at the screen and somehow I lose track of what I’m doing because I’m thinking about stuff at home, or whether a bill got paid, or… I don’t know, random things.

Then I have to stop and recount the drawer, or I’ll catch some small mistake and feel kind of stupid about it. It’s not like I can’t do my job, but my mind wanders off at bad times.
Have you noticed a loss of energy or feel fatigued, even after resting or sleeping well?

Yeah… that’s actually kind of the main reason I came in. I just feel worn out almost every day. Like even if I get what should be a full night’s sleep, I get up and my body’s already dragging, and my head feels kind of heavy going into my cashier shift.

And it’s weird because standing at the register isn’t like construction work or anything, though people do act like coupons are a federal case sometimes… but yeah, I feel tired before I even really start.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately—like eating less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Not really, no. I mean, I haven’t been keeping track on a scale or anything. My pants fit about the same, I think.

Food-wise… I still eat, but sometimes I’ll just grab whatever’s easy from work or forget lunch until later, but that’s kind of always been me. Like if it’s busy and there’s a line, I’m not thinking about a sandwich, I’m thinking about getting people out of there before someone starts complaining about the self-checkout again. But no, I haven’t noticed losing weight or eating way less on purpose or anything like that.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest in most things or aren’t getting any pleasure out of stuff you usually enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with people?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in everything. I still like the usual stuff when I actually get around to it.

Like, I’ll watch something or mess around on my phone, and it’s fine. Sometimes I don’t start anything because by the time I get home I’m just kind of… done, and then I end up scrolling through videos about people restoring old tools, which is weirdly relaxing. My cousin got into that too, actually, he bought this rusty old vise at a yard sale and acted like he found buried treasure.

But, uh… no, I don’t think it’s like I can’t enjoy things anymore. I haven’t really noticed that.
Have you found it harder to focus on tasks, make decisions, or remember things lately?

Yeah, a bit. Mostly at work. Like I’ll be at the register, looking right at the screen, and then somehow my mind is off thinking about stuff at home or whether a bill got paid, and I lose my place.

It’s not like I forget where I am or anything, but I’ll have to recount the drawer or I’ll catch some small mistake and think, “How did I miss that?” Which is annoying, because the screen is literally in front of me. And then someone’s asking if they can use an expired coupon from 2019, and I’m trying to act like I’m fully present, but my brain’s already three streets away.
Have you noticed a significant loss of interest or pleasure in activities you usually enjoy, even when you have the chance to do them?

I don’t think so, no. Like if I actually have time and sit down to do something I like, I can still enjoy it. I might not always get around to it, but that’s more just… I don’t know, the day gets away from me.

Like last weekend I was going to watch this movie, and then I spent half an hour trying to find the remote, and somehow ended up cleaning out that little drawer where all the batteries and takeout menus go. Everybody has one of those, right? But once I actually put something on, it was fine. So… no, I wouldn’t say I’ve had a big loss of interest or anything.
Have you felt down or really unmotivated most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

I mean… not most of the day every day, no, I don’t think so. I have days where I’m dragging and I don’t feel like doing much, but I wouldn’t say it’s been like two straight weeks where I’m just down all day.

Some mornings are harder, but then I get moving or something distracts me. Like at work, there’s always some random thing happening, someone arguing about a price tag or the card reader acting up, so you don’t really get to sit there and think too much. Well, unless it’s slow, then time feels like it’s not moving at all.

But yeah… I don’t think it’s been that constant.
Have you found that you don’t take pleasure or interest in almost anything, even things you usually enjoy, for days at a time?

I don’t think it’s like that, no. I mean, I can get sidetracked and not do the thing I planned to do, but if I actually get into it, I usually still like it.

Like I’ll tell myself I’m gonna play a game or watch something, and then suddenly I’m checking if the laundry’s done or moving stuff around on the coffee table, and then I’m standing there wondering why I came into the kitchen. But that’s not really the same as not enjoying anything, I guess.

So… no, I haven’t noticed days where nothing feels enjoyable. At least not that I can think of.
Have you had several days in a row where you felt down or really unmotivated most of the day, even when there wasn’t a clear reason like being tired or having a bad day at work?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think so, not several days in a row like that. I mean, I’ll have a day where I feel kind of blah and don’t want to do anything, but usually I can point to something, like I slept weird or work was annoying, or I just had one of those days where everything feels like it takes twice as long.

The “no clear reason” part is hard, because sometimes there is a reason but it’s stupid, like I couldn’t find my keys and then I’m irritated for an hour. I have this little bowl by the door that’s supposed to be for keys, but then it ends up with receipts and coins and those little store loyalty cards nobody uses anymore.

But, uh… to answer you, I don’t think I’ve had several days in a row where I was down or unmotivated most of the day for no reason.

Over the past two weeks, have there been several days in a row where you didn’t feel like doing anything—even things you usually enjoy—where it didn’t seem like it would be worth the effort, even if you weren’t tired or having a bad day?

I don’t think so… not several days in a row like that. I mean, sometimes I’ll look at something I usually like doing and think, “Ugh, that sounds like a lot,” but then it’s usually because I’m already kind of worn out or I’ve got other stuff in my head.

Like even picking what to watch can turn into this whole thing, because there’s too many choices, and then I end up scrolling for twenty minutes and watching some video about how people restore old furniture. I don’t even own furniture worth restoring, unless you count this wobbly little side table I keep meaning to fix.

But, sorry—your question was more like if nothing felt worth the effort for days, even without a reason. No, I haven’t really noticed that happening.

Over the past two weeks, have you had a period of time where you felt down, uninterested, or unmotivated most of the day, nearly every day, even when there wasn’t an obvious reason like being tired or stressed?

I don’t think so… I mean, I’ve had parts of days where I feel kind of flat or I don’t want to start anything, but “most of the day, nearly every day” sounds stronger than what I’ve noticed.

Sometimes I think I’m just stuck in that mode where I’m like, okay, I should do something, and then I start messing with my phone or I reorganize a drawer for no real reason. I did that with my junk drawer the other day—found like three old batteries and a takeout menu from a place that closed, I think, two years ago.

But, sorry—no, I don’t think I’ve had a stretch like that over the last couple weeks where I was down or uninterested most of the day for no obvious reason.
Have you experienced days where you had little to no interest or pleasure in everything you did, even in things you usually enjoy, for most of the day, nearly every day?

I don’t think so. Like, I can have a day where stuff doesn’t sound fun, but “everything” and “most of the day, nearly every day” feels like more than what’s been happening.

I still get interested in things, it’s just sometimes I take forever to start them. Like I’ll mean to watch a show I actually like, then I spend half the night looking up what else that actor was in, and somehow I’m reading about some movie from 1998 I’ve never seen. But that’s not really the same as not enjoying anything.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed days like that.

Over the past few months, have you had a stretch of at least two weeks where you felt down or uninterested in things most of the day, nearly every day, even when there wasn’t a clear reason like being stressed or tired?

Over the past few months… I don’t think I’ve had a two-week stretch like that. I mean, I have days where I’m kind of blah or I don’t feel like doing much, but it doesn’t really stick around most of the day every day.

Sometimes it’s more like I get stuck deciding what to do, and then suddenly I’ve spent an hour looking at reviews for something I wasn’t even planning to buy—like a toaster oven, even though mine works fine. So it can look like I’m not interested in anything, but I don’t think it’s that exactly.

So, no… not that I’ve noticed, anyway.

Some mornings are harder, but then I get moving or something distracts me. Like at work, there’s always some random thing happening, someone arguing about a price tag or the card reader acting up, so you don’t really get to sit there and think too much. Well, unless it’s slow, then time feels like it’s not moving at all.

But yeah… I don’t think it’s been that constant.

patient.answer:
I don’t think it’s like that, no. I mean, I can get sidetracked and not do the thing I planned to do, but if I actually get into it, I usually still like it.

Like I’ll tell myself I’m gonna play a game or watch something, and then suddenly I’m checking if the laundry’s done or moving stuff around on the coffee table, and then I’m standing there wondering why I came into the kitchen. But that’s not really the same as not enjoying anything, I guess.

So… no, I haven’t noticed days where nothing feels enjoyable. At least not that I can think of.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure. I don’t think so, not several days in a row like that. I mean, I’ll have a day where I feel kind of blah and don’t want to do anything, but usually I can point to something, like I slept weird or work was annoying, or I just had one of those days where everything feels like it takes twice as long.

The “no clear reason” part is hard, because sometimes there is a reason but it’s stupid, like I couldn’t find my keys and then I’m irritated for an hour. I have this little bowl by the door that’s supposed to be for keys, but then it ends up with receipts and coins and those little store loyalty cards nobody uses anymore.

But, uh… to answer you, I don’t think I’ve had several days in a row where I was down or unmotivated most of the day for no reason.

Like even picking what to watch can turn into this whole thing, because there’s too many choices, and then I end up scrolling for twenty minutes and watching some video about how people restore old furniture. I don’t even own furniture worth restoring, unless you count this wobbly little side table I keep meaning to fix.

But, sorry—your question was more like if nothing felt worth the effort for days, even without a reason. No, I haven’t really noticed that happening.

I did that with my junk drawer the other day—found like three old batteries and a takeout menu from a place that closed, I think, two years ago.

But, sorry—no, I don’t think I’ve had a stretch like that over the last couple weeks where I was down or uninterested most of the day for no obvious reason.
